questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=-3x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{n}.$

$\,{a}_{n}=$ {{field-1}}
for $n\ge 1$
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-3x$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{a}_{n}=-\frac{6}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }x\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-\frac{6}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{6}{\pi }(\frac{1}{n}[x\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{1}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{6}{n\pi }((\pi \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+\frac{1}{n}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =-\frac{6}{n\pi }(0+\frac{1}{n}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{6(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi ))}{{n}^{2}\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{6(1-(-1)^{n})}{\pi {n}^{2}}.
$$

questions.problem:
Let $F(x)=5x+2$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ Select the correct missing parts in the Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function $F(x)$ below.

$$
f(x)∼(2+\frac{5}{2}\pi )+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot {{field-2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=5x+2$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(5x+2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x+2\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{1}{n}[(5x+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{5}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{2}{n\pi }(((5\pi +2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+\frac{5}{n}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{2}{n\pi }(0+\frac{5}{n}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{10(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-1)}{{n}^{2}\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{10((-1)^{n}-1)}{\pi {n}^{2}}.
$$

Finally, the Fourier cosine series is

$$
f(x)∼(2+\frac{5}{2}\pi )+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{10((-1)^{n}-1)}{\pi {n}^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=12{x}^{2}-\pi $ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=12{x}^{2}-\pi $ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(12{x}^{2}-\pi )\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[12\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-\pi x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(4{\pi }^{3}-{\pi }^{2})-0 \\  & =2\pi (4\pi -1).\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 2π(4π−1)

questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }(1-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 4π
